svg.text: Screws under the deck pull rods and crosshead down; the force loop is closed; what leaves the die falls into the pot.
4 kN peak · 600 mm stroke · 750 W servo, 1 belt, 2 ball screws 20 × 5
cutting 50 mm/s · rapid 150 mm/s · rods Ø 25 see 4 MPa
tube 100 × 100 × 260 · stored energy at break-through ≈ 0.5 J
no drive and no rod collar above the open pot
Close-up: 6 mm dice from an onion
Top view: rods on the diagonal
Rods ±190 mm in x and ±120 mm in y about the die: the 4 kN loop has no bending.
the curve tells: empty, jam, bone, done

g.text: 1/5 Load: the handler tips peeled onion halves into the tube and sets the bought pusher head on top
2/5 Rapid: the servo turns both screws through one belt; the yoke, the two rods and the crosshead come down at 150 mm/s
3/5 Cut: 50 mm/s, about 1–2 kN; the reaction runs round a closed, symmetric loop (red) — no C-frame, no bending
4/5 Through: the pusher fingers clear the blade grid; the dice have already fallen straight into the pot below
5/5 Return: the crosshead goes back up to z 1 800; nothing of the drive stands above the open pot
